messages:
deploy-bot: initiating rollout release=2026.01.15 pipeline=main canary=alpha migration=20260115_v03 step=apply-ddl
marcos (sre): alerts: checkout 500s increasing on canary-alpha at 03:12 UTC, traces show SQL errors referencing missing column
janet (oncall): I'm on it, pulling logs and psql session info
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0081 created severity=sev2 notified=oncall,db,release
katie (release): canary auto-paused by health-check: reason=5xx>threshold at 03:13:05
marcos (sre): app trace snippet: `ERROR SQLState=42703: column customer.loyalty_tier does not exist`
devon (db): looking at migration manager: migration 20260115_v03 status=running, current step=ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN loyalty_tier varchar(20); pid=1210
infra-bot: current db connections: total=120 active=34 idle=86
janet (oncall): tail app logs: several services calling `SELECT loyalty_tier FROM customers WHERE id=$1` -> 500s
katie (release): what are our quick mitigations? 1) abort migration (dangerous), 2) flip flag to stop new code path, 3) kill blocking session after notifying analytics
marcos (sre): recommend feature-flag first + pause rollout. We should avoid terminating DB sessions unless confirmed by analytics. Runbook: migrate-runbook#section-3b
janet (oncall): flipping flag `feature.loyalty_v2` to false for canary routes now via flags-api
janet (oncall): command: `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api -d '{"key":"feature.loyalty_v2","enabled":false,"scope":"canary-alpha"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer ***"`
marcos (sre): errors on canary drop to baseline ~1m after flag flip, good signal
devon (db): but migration process still waiting on lock. `psql` shows blocking chain:
```
 pid  | state  | waiting | query
------+--------+---------+-------------------------
 888  | idle   | t       | COPY (SELECT * FROM customers) TO '/mnt/exports/customers.csv'
 1210 | active | t       | ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN loyalty_tier varchar(20)
```
analytics-oncall: export job export-20260115 initiated by analytics-scheduled, currently running; paged analytics oncall (paging elie)
katie (release): pausing rollout to avoid wider impact; release paused at 03:16 UTC
incident-bot: deployment paused by katie at 03:16:21 UTC
devon (db): reached analytics-oncall, they can stop the export safely, ETA 4m
janet (oncall): agree with terminating export after they cancel, prefer graceful stop to minimize disruption
analytics-oncall: cancel requested, job will stop in ~30s
infra-bot: export job terminated by analytics-runner at 03:20:12 UTC
devon (db): executing `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(888);` to free lock. audit log generated
incident-bot: Audit: user=devon action=pg_terminate_backend target_pid=888
marcos (sre): migration picked up lock and completed ALTER at 03:22:05 UTC, migration state=applied
katie (release): recommending resuming canary at 2% then 10% if stable. resuming at 2% now
janet (oncall): monitoring metrics: errors remain flat, P95 latency OK
marcos (sre): after 15m at 2% and 10m at 10% we promoted to 100%, no recurrence of missing-column errors
nora (cs): customer note drafted: "Between 03:12 and 03:22 UTC a small percentage of checkout requests in canary experienced failures due to a release migration that was blocked by a running export job. We mitigated by disabling the new feature flag, stopping the export, completing the migration, and resuming the rollout. We are following up with a postmortem." will post to status page after confirm
katie (release): observed approx 0.02% aborted checkouts during window; no data corruption, orders that failed were retried by users or retried by our client side logic
marcos (sre): post-incident action items: - add pre-deploy check for long-running COPY/export sessions - update deploy pipeline to detect exclusive lock blockers and fail fast - change DDL pattern to create NULL column first + backfill asynchronously - docs: remind analytics to schedule large exports during maintenance windows or use snapshot export technique
janet (oncall): I'm handing over oncall to marcos for next 2 hours. Handoff notes: monitor checkout 5xx and DB lock stats, check alert rule INC-2026-0081 for 1h
marcos (sre): taking over oncall. I'll draft the postmortem and tag devon + katie for DB/release sections
incident-bot: INC-2026-0081 resolved at 03:45:20 UTC (timeline: start 03:12 UTC, mitigation 03:14-03:22 UTC, resolution 03:45 UTC)
nora (cs): status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-2026-0081 and customers notified; no escalations so far
katie (release): thanks team, nice coordination. closing thread :white_check_mark:
